blocks.text: Deuteronomy 10 belongs to the book's movement from remembered wilderness failure toward renewed covenant instruction. Moses recounts the replacement tablets, the ark, priestly service, and his intercession before turning to what the Lord requires: fear, love, service, obedience, and a circumcised heart. The exhortation joins worship of the great and impartial God to concrete love for the sojourner. In the larger book, this remembered history leads into covenant laws, consequences, renewal, succession, song, blessing, and Moses' death; the chapter is therefore neither bare recollection nor an isolated list of duties.
